title: A. R. Rahman Spent Three Years on 'Ramayana' Music, Turned Down 10–12 Films
excerpt: At IFFI in Panaji, the composer said he set aside almost everything else for Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic, co-composing with Hans Zimmer — some pieces went through 12–13 versions.
body:
• A. R. Rahman told a press conference at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Panaji that he has spent nearly three years on the music of Nitesh Tiwari's two-part "Ramayana" and turned down 10–12 film projects to stay focused on it.
  • Rahman is composing the score with German composer Hans Zimmer; some pieces went through 12–13 versions, including the "Ravana Tandav," which was worked on in different languages.
  • The Hindi-language epic stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana; its first part reached cinemas at Diwali 2026.
  • Rahman was at IFFI for Bharat Bala's "Banaras," for which he composed the music and serves as executive producer; the festival concludes on November 28.

A. R. Rahman has given three years to one film. Speaking at a press conference at the International Film Festival of India in Panaji, the Oscar-winning composer said he devoted nearly three years to the music of "Ramayana," Nitesh Tiwari's two-part adaptation of the epic, and turned down 10 to 12 film projects so he could stay inside its world, PTI reported.

"We've been doing 'Ramayana' music for three years, the themes and everything. And some of them have like, 12–13 versions. The 'Ravana Tandav' actually had 12–13 versions and then we finally found a version which everybody liked."

— A. R. Rahman, at IFFI

"The process was beautiful. Because of 'Ramayana', I left almost 10–12 movies, just to be in the zone. Many, many important big filmmakers I left. And I'm proud of it," Rahman said, in remarks also reported by Movie Talkies. Asked how he chooses projects despite a demanding schedule, he said he takes up work only when he feels a strong connection with it: "I only accept when I really love a project and I enjoy it, it nourishes my artistic sense and my whole team gets excited."

A score built with Hans Zimmer

Rahman is composing "Ramayana" with Hans Zimmer, the German composer behind "The Lion King," "Dune" and "Interstellar" scores — a pairing that puts an Indian epic's music in the hands of two of the most decorated film composers working today. Rahman spoke at IFFI about the challenge of bringing together traditional Indian music and contemporary global sounds, and about drawing influences from cultures that appear geographically distant. The "Ravana Tandav" example shows the working method: the same composition reworked more than a dozen times, in different languages, before the team settled on a version.

The film, and where to watch it

"Ramayana" is a Hindi-language, two-part cinematic adaptation of the epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita and Yash plays Ravana, with Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Hanuman. The first part reached cinemas at Diwali 2026 and is in theatres now; for diaspora audiences, Rahman's remarks are a reminder of the scale of the production behind a film many have already seen — three years of music work, most of it before a frame reached the screen.

Why he was at IFFI

Rahman was speaking after the screening of Bharat Bala's "Banaras," a Hindi drama set against the backdrop of Hindustani classical music and the cultural landscape of Varanasi. The film stars Neeraj Kabi, Shahana Goswami and Abhishek Banerjee, alongside Chhaya Kadam; Rahman composed its music and also serves as an executive producer. "This film was a great opportunity. Not every time does a filmmaker come with a musical subject, where the lead singer is singing a song based on a musical family and original music," he said. IFFI concludes on November 28.
